_README: Single source of truth for every dimension in the enclosure. All values are millimetres. Component dimensions are the ones confirmed against the physical parts; the rest are design choices. Every key here is consumed by model.py -- the ones beginning with _ are documentation and are stripped before the model sees them, so there are no dead parameters to mislead you.

sensor._active_area_note: The reading face stands this far proud of the body. It caps features.bezel_lip: any more plastic than this and the lid covers the sensing surface, which a capacitive sensor cannot read through.
sensor._cable_note: The six-wire pigtail leaves the back of the module and runs under it, through the notch in the seat, to the board.

board._model: ESP32-S3, dual USB-C (native USB plus the UART bridge)
board._height_note: Full envelope, tallest point to lowest. This is the single largest number in the build and it sets the height of the whole enclosure -- see docs/enclosure.md.
board._usb_offset_note: Only the native USB port gets an opening; the UART bridge stays behind the wall. That is why the opening is off-centre. Setting this to 0 centres the port and takes about 3 mm off the width -- see the size the build script reports. Flip the sign if the opening comes out on the wrong side.

fit._window_clearance_note: Per side, around the sensor's active area.
fit._lid_clearance_note: Per-side gap between the lid edge and the recess. 0.15 is a friction fit on a well-tuned FDM printer; open it to 0.25 if the lid will not seat.
fit._port_edge_margin_note: Wall left between the USB opening and the corner of the cavity. The enclosure widens if the off-centre port would otherwise break out through the corner.

shell._lid_ledge_note: Width of the shelf the lid rests on; the wall above the shelf is (wall - lid_ledge) thick.
shell._board_standoff_note: Height of the posts under the PCB. Also the gap the sensor's pigtail uses to reach the board.
shell._part_gap_note: Between the board pocket and the sensor pocket, sized for the pigtail's bend radius.
shell._board_long_axis_note: Which way the board's 25 mm side runs. The USB-C port is on its 18 mm edge, so this also decides which wall the port opens through: "y" puts it in a side wall and keeps the longest outside dimension down to 46.4 mm, "x" puts it in the end wall so the thing plugs in along its own length like a USB stick, at 53.4 mm long.
shell._square_note: Pad the shorter axis until the footprint is square. 46.4 x 46.4 x 13.0 is the smallest square these two parts fit in without stacking the sensor back on the board. Build the rectangular version with: build.py --no-square --board-long-axis x

features._post_note: Four posts under the PCB corners, inset from the pocket edge so they land on board rather than on castellations.
features._sensor_seat_note: Radial width of the ring that lifts the sensor against the underside of the lid. Wide enough that the ring stays rigid at its full height.
features._bezel_lip_note: Thickness of the lid ring that overlaps the module's shoulder and holds it down. Must not exceed sensor.active_area_height.
features._guide_note: L-shaped ribs at the board pocket corners. The posts carry the board's weight; these stop it sliding, which matters once the cavity is larger than the board.
features._pry_notch_note: Scallop in the rim that lets a fingernail lift the lid; the shell has no screws.
